name: When should I consider replacing a section of drywall instead of repairing it?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider replacing a section of drywall instead of repairing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Consider replacing a section of drywall when the damage is extensive, such as large holes over 6 inches in diameter, severe water damage that has compromised the board's integrity (making it soft, moldy, or crumbling), or widespread impact damage. While repairs are often feasible, replacing a section can be more time-efficient and cost-effective than attempting to salvage severely damaged drywall, ensuring a more stable and aesthetically pleasing result for painting.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace drywall for extensive damage like large holes, severe water damage, or widespread impact, as it can be more efficient and provide a better outcome than repair.
